paper: P23 Order-six torsion in an ordered graph configuration space
policy: Published external results are precise explicit parameters; own graph hypotheses and concrete certificate identities remain internal proof obligations.
status: explicit_parameters_only; no axioms and no sorry introduced

dependencies.name: Prue–Scrimshaw stable equivalence, specialized H2 consequence

primary_sources.title: Abrams’s stable equivalence for graph braid groups

original_quantifiers.graph: Every finite connected graph G, viewed as a one-dimensional CW complex. The introductory stable-equivalence statement additionally assumes at least n vertices; the application satisfies this stronger version.
original_quantifiers.condition_A: For every pair of distinct vertices u,v with degrees unequal to 2, every edge path from u to v has at least n−1 edges.
original_quantifiers.condition_B: For every vertex v, every homotopically essential edge path from v to itself has at least n+1 edges.
original_quantifiers.conclusion: The ordered configuration space C^n(G) deformation retracts onto the ordered discretized subspace D^n(G).
original_quantifiers.homology_invariance: For every pair of spaces X,Y, every homotopy equivalence f:X→Y and every degree q, the induced integral singular-homology map f_* is an isomorphism.

specialization.graph: Paper23.subdividedGraph, with 32 vertices and 39 edges; its actual quotient realization is used.
specialization.map: Paper23.ExternalTopology.discretizedInclusionMap; inclusionHomologyMorphism is the pinned mathlib singularHomologyFunctor map of this exact inclusion; inclusionHomologyMap is its additive homomorphism.
proved_graph_conditions: GraphGirth.special_walk_length (all walks between distinct special vertices have length at least 3)
specialization.condition_B_encoding: The Lean sufficient condition is that every conventional SimpleGraph cycle has length at least 5, proved via the stronger girth-six theorem. The standard one-dimensional-CW interpretation/reduction of edge loops converts this to the original non-nullhomotopic closed-path condition. That standard topological interpretation is part of this disclosed specialization, not an additional graph computation assumed from the external input.

missing_formalization: Prue–Scrimshaw deformation retraction theorem for these actual ordered topological subspaces
Singular-homology homotopy invariance for the pinned mathlib singularHomologyFunctor
Standard graph edge-loop/cycle interpretation used to express source condition B through conventional girth
does_not_supply: Any cycle, bounding chain, detecting cocycle, certificate identity, or order-six conclusion

dependencies.name: Oriented ordered cubical CW-chain identification and cellular-to-singular comparison

primary_sources.author: Allen Hatcher
primary_sources.title: Algebraic Topology
primary_sources.theorem: Theorem 2.35, p.139; cellular boundary discussion immediately following

primary_sources.title: Abrams’s stable equivalence for graph braid groups
primary_sources.location: Introduction: ordered D^n(G) has the cubical CW subcomplex structure; proof of Lemma 2.2 describes labelled disjoint product cells

original_quantifiers.cellular_comparison: For every CW complex X and every degree q, its integral cellular homology is naturally isomorphic to its integral singular homology.
original_quantifiers.cubical_specialization: For a finite regular cubical subcomplex with an orientation on each cube, the free abelian oriented-cell chain groups with the incidence face differential are the cellular chain groups. Changing cube orientations by signs gives a chain-isomorphic complex.

specialization.space: The actual ordered subspace Paper23.DiscretizedSourceSpace, consisting of four labelled graph-cell coordinates with pairwise disjoint closures.
specialization.chain_source: Paper23.orderedCubicalComplex on Cubical.Chains 3, Cubical.Chains 2, Cubical.Chains 1; these are supported free integer chains on valid labelled cubes, with Cubical.differential and the increasing-moving-edge orientation.
specialization.source_homology: Paper23.DiscreteH₂, the actual cycles/boundaries quotient of orderedCubicalComplex.
specialization.target_homology: Paper23.IntegralHomology 2 DiscretizedSourceSpace, using pinned mathlib singular homology.
already_proved_support: The actual source-cell and topological-subspace definitions
specialization.explicitly_included_external_adapter: Construction of the regular cubical CW structure on this topological D4, identification of its cellular chain groups and attaching incidence signs with this concrete free ordered-cube model, and the resulting comparison to pinned mathlib singular homology. The supporting combinatorial definitions do not claim that this CW-chain adapter has been constructed in Lean.

missing_formalization: CW structure/characteristic maps and cellular-chain adapter for this actual finite cubical subcomplex
A general cellular/singular comparison theorem integrated with the pinned mathlib singular-homology definition
does_not_supply: Any direct torsion or main-theorem conclusion

proved_separately: Explicit subdivision homeomorphism and induced ordered-configuration/singular-homology isomorphism in Paper23.Subdivision
Algebraic exact order-six argument in Paper23.CertificateAlgebra

Explicit homeomorphism from the eight-vertex fifteen-edge simple graph presentation to the original graph, and induced ordered-configuration/singular-homology equivalences, in Paper23.SimplePresentation
